..(This Evening Through Tuesday)
Issued at 213 PM MDT Tue Sep 8 2026

Our main weather concern this week will remain warm to hot, dry,
and at times breezy conditions resulting in elevated to near-
critical fire weather. On the synoptic scale...a somewhat 
"undulating" zonal flow will dominate today through Friday, with 
embedded shortwave troughs brushing across the region this 
evening and again Wednesday evening. This evening's feature will 
be the stronger of the two, supporting already-observed 30-40 MPH 
wind gusts up across the northwestern South Dakota plains. Enough 
lift may be present with the trough/weak frontal feature to induce
development of a few showers during the first half of the 
overnight tonight roughly north of a line from Gillette to Faith 
(as reflected with actually decent consensus across nearly all 
current CAM guidance), despite the best precip potential focusing 
well to our north over Montana and North Dakota. This scenario was
not well captured by the NBM, so blended in some high-res 
guidance and broadbrushed light 10-30% PoPs tonight up across this
region to cover any development. Instability seems limited, and 
have left thunder out of the forecast for now. Regardless, 
significant impacts are not expected from this activity with very 
little QPF. Wednesday evening's feature is actually 
sharper/stronger in the upper levels of the atmosphere, but weak 
at the surface, and is currently expected to cross the region dry 
with little to no impact. The hottest temperatures of the week are
expected Thursday and Friday, returning to the 90s.

Friday, long-range deterministic models continue to key in on two
primary features. The first will be a large low pressure center
crossing Canada to our north, which will assist in tightening the
pressure gradient and increasing northwesterly winds Friday 
afternoon and evening (gusts 25-40 MPH across the region). This
will especially be a fire weather concern...not expecting Wind
Advisory-level winds at this time. Some hint of troughing 
extending southwestward from this parent low may also help support
some shower/thunderstorm potential starting late Friday afternoon
into the first part of Friday night, although confidence in this 
period is low. Meaningful or widespread QPF seems unlikely. The 
second main feature will be a second closed low rotating down the 
back side of this Canadian parent low and then swinging 
eastward/inland across the northern Rockies. Moisture advecting in
on southwest flow ahead of this low, along with increasing upper-
level support, will bring us a better chance of more organized 
precipitation sometime in the Saturday/Sunday/Monday timeframe, 
although amounts are still very much in question at this range. 
(WPC guidance currently supports about one-quarter inch, with 
potentially higher amounts over the south-central South Dakota 
plains.) This system will moisten up our relative humidity values 
taking the edge off fire weather concerns, and COULD spell at 
least a temporary end to the heat! NBM high temperatures currently
top out at 70 to 80 degrees Saturday, and 65 to 75 degrees Sunday
and Monday, with overnight lows in the 40s through the period. 
The overall magnitude of the cooler air during this period has 
perhaps moderated a bit in the guidance over the past 24 hours, 
although Saturday itself has trended a bit cooler. Keep in mind 
that our actual eventual temperatures (and QPF amounts) will be 
tied to the strength and track of this low. Looking at 500mb 
height cluster analysis...some differences between clusters are 
noted Saturday in the position of the incoming low/trough axis (as
far east as Idaho but as far west as off the Oregon coast), with 
EOF patterns confirming the majority of model uncertainty is 
currently tied to speed/position of the low. Most clusters 
currently remain dry or modest with respect to QPF. Similar 
overall observations by Sunday, but the stakes will be higher at 
that point with the low in much closer proximity to Wyoming and 
South Dakota, meaning significant differences in both potential 
temperatures and QPF. 2 clusters (about 65% of the ensemble space)
support over 0.25" of QPF and cooler temperatures tied to a 
faster low, while another 2 (about 35% of members) support much 
drier conditions tied to a further west low with significantly 
warmer temperatures remaining in place. (Thus, there is a small 
chance...currently about 35 percent...that our pattern change 
could be delayed and Saturday's forecast could trend toward 
another warmer and continued elevated fire weather day.) By 
Sunday night and Monday, confidence increases much more 
comfortably in cooler temperatures and showers over the region. No
deviations were made from NBM and WPC guidance in the forecast 
from Friday onward at this time.
